title: BSA-seq in Maize
author: Harry Klein
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qyedxte

steps.title: Upload sequencing data via FTP
steps.instruction: Transfer raw sequencing files to Galaxy using an FTP client (e.g., CyberDuck). Galaxy limits single uploads to 2 GB and provides 250 GB total storage per user; delete files if needed to stay under this limit. Also upload the B73 reference genome downloaded from maizesequence.org. After the FTP transfer finishes, in Galaxy click “choose FTP file” under Get Data > Upload File to add the files to your history.

steps.title: Assess sequencing quality with FastQC
steps.instruction: Run FastQC on each sequencing file to evaluate read quality and decide on a quality cutoff. Contaminant list and submodules are optional.

steps.title: Convert FASTQ format if needed
steps.instruction: If Bowtie2 will be used, ensure files are in fastqsanger format. Convert any fastq files using the FASTQ Groomer tool in Galaxy.

steps.title: Concatenate multiple sequencing files (optional)
steps.instruction: Merge split Illumina output files for a sample using the Unix command `cat` to create a single FASTQ file.

steps.title: Map reads to B73 reference with Bowtie2
steps.instruction: Build a genome from your history using the B73 v4 reference, select paired‑end or single‑end reads, and run Bowtie2 with default options. Mapping typically takes 4–24 hours depending on data size.

steps.title: Call variants using Samtools Mpileup
steps.instruction: Run Samtools mpileup, selecting the B73 genome from your history, disable genotype‑likelihood computation (output pileup), and output base positions on reads.

steps.title: Filter Mpileup by coverage with Samtools
steps.instruction: Use Samtools filter‑pileup plugin to remove SNPs below a coverage cutoff. Set cutoff = 2 for low‑coverage data (≈2×) and cutoff = 8 for high‑coverage data (>15×). Also print the total number of differences.

steps.title: Trim low-quality reads with Trimmomatic
steps.instruction: Run Trimmomatic on your data with a sliding window of 4 and a minimum Phred quality score of 20 (Galaxy defaults). Select the files and execute.

steps.title: Calculate alignment coverage with Samtools Flagstat
steps.instruction: Run Samtools flagstat on the alignment BAM to obtain the number of reads mapped to the reference, which is used for downstream coverage calculations.

steps.title: Generate Varscan SNP/Indel VCFs
steps.instruction: Run the Varscan plugin on the filtered Mpileup. Use a coverage cutoff of 2 for low‑coverage data (≤15×) and set the minimum homozygote frequency to 0.99. Also generate an indel VCF for later marker design.

steps.title: Reformat filtered pileup for R analysis
steps.instruction: Process the filtered pileup with a series of awk commands to compute allele frequencies and produce a CSV ready for R.

substeps.instruction: cd to the directory containing the filtered.pileup file.
For each chromosome, extract lines and compute f_variant = $13/$12: `awk '{if ($1==<chrom>) print $0}' filtered.pileup | awk '{$14=$13/$12; print $0}' > chrX.freq.pileup`.
Filter for f_variant > 0.5: `awk '{if($14>0.5)print $0}' chrX.freq.pileup > chrX_0.5.pileup`.
Print position, ref, alt, f_variant, coverage: `awk '{print $2,$3,$5,$14,$11}' chrX_0.5.pileup > chrX_filter.pileup`.
Convert ambiguous bases to canonical A,T,G,C: `awk '$3~/[Aa]/{$3="A"} $3~/[Tt]/{$3="T"} $3~/[Gg]/{$3="G"} $3~/[Cc]/{$3="C"} 1' chrX_filter.pileup > chrX_filter2.pileup`.
Optional EMS‑only filter: `awk '{if ($2=="C" && $3~/[Tt]/) print $0; else if ($2=="G" && $3~/[Aa]/) print $0}' chrX_filter.pileup > chrX_filter2.pileup`.
Optional second conversion step (if needed): `awk '$3~/[Aa]/{$3="A"} $3~/[Tt]/{$3="T"} 1' chrX_filter2.pileup > chrX_filter3.pileup`.
Convert to CSV: `awk '{print $1","$2","$3","$4","$5}' chrX_filter3.pileup > chrX_EMS.csv`.
Create a header file (e.g., `header.csv` containing `position,ref,alt,f_variant,coverage`) and prepend it: `cat header.csv chrX_EMS.csv > chrX_final.csv`.

steps.title: Load required R packages
steps.instruction: In RStudio, run `install.packages('dplyr')`, then `library(dplyr)` and `library(ggplot2)`.

steps.title: Import data files into R
steps.instruction: Read the processed CSVs and optional background files into R. Example: `chr1_final <- read.csv('path/to/chr1_final.csv')`. If WT or HapMap position files are single‑column, read them with `read.table` and add a header: `colnames(WT_chr1) <- c('position')`.

steps.title: Optional: Filter by coverage SD
steps.instruction: Filter SNPs to keep only those with coverage within ±1 SD of the mean (e.g., `chr1_coverage100 = "lowerlimit" & coverage <= "upperlimit"`).

steps.title: Plot homozygous SNPs with ggplot2
steps.instruction: Create a histogram of homozygous SNPs (f_variant ≥ 0.99) to locate the chromosome with the highest SNP density.

substeps.instruction: Initial plot: `ggplot(subset(chr1_final_NoWTHapmap, f_variant>=0.99), aes(x=position)) + geom_histogram(binwidth=1000000) + expand_limits(y=c(0, max(chr1_final_NoWTHapmap$position))) + scale_x_continuous(breaks=round(seq(min(0), max(chr1_final_NoWTHapmap$position), by=20000000), 10000000)) + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=70, hjust=1)) + theme_bw()`.
Adjust y‑axis for the chromosome with most SNPs (e.g., `expand_limits(y=c(0,1000))`).
The dense SNP region indicates the mapping interval.

steps.title: Prepare Varscan files for SnpEff
steps.instruction: Split the Varscan VCF by chromosome, extract the mapping region, remove background SNPs, and keep only EMS‑type changes.

substeps.instruction: Extract chromosome: `awk '{if($1=="<chrom>") print $0}' Varscan.vcf > chr1.vcf`.
Extract mapping region (e.g., positions ≥40,000,000): `awk '{if($2>=40000000 && $2<=<upper>) print $0}' chr1.vcf > chr1_mapping_region.vcf`.

Remove background SNPs using the cluster scheduler: `bsub -o chr1_mapping_region_NoWT.vcf -e background.err -n 1 -R rusage[mem=4096] -W 120 -q short grep -wvFf background_SNPs.txt chr1_mapping_region.vcf` or alternatively `awk 'FNR==NR {hash[$0]; next} !($2 in hash)' Hapmap_chr1.txt chr1_mapping_region.vcf > chr1_NoHapmap.vcf`.
Keep only EMS variants (C→T or G→A): `awk '{if ($4=="C" && $5=="T") print $0; else if ($4=="G" && $5=="A") print $0}' chr1_NoHapmap.vcf > chr1_NoHapmap_EMS.vcf`.

steps.title: Run SnpEff on filtered EMS SNPs
steps.instruction: Build a SnpEff database for maize version 4, move the filtered EMS VCF into the SnpEff folder, and annotate.

substeps.instruction: Follow the SnpEff manual (http://snpeff.sourceforge.net/SnpEff_manual.html) to build the Zmv4 database.
Run: `java -jar snpEff.jar Zmv4 chr1_NoHapmap_EMS.vcf`.
Submit to the cluster: `bsub -o vns_SNPeff.vcf -e vns_SNPeff.err -n 4 -R rusage[mem=4096] -W 120 -q short java -jar snpEff.jar Zmv4 chr1_NoHapmap_EMS.vcf`.

steps.title: Filter SnpEff results by effect and homozygosity
steps.instruction: Separate moderate and high impact SNPs and keep only homozygous calls.

substeps.instruction: Extract moderate effects: `grep MODERATE vns_SNPeff.vcf > MODERATE.vcf`.
Extract high effects: `grep HIGH vns_SNPeff.vcf > HIGH.vcf`.
Select homozygous SNPs: `grep HOM=1 MODERATE.vcf > MODERATE_HOM.vcf` and `grep HOM=1 HIGH.vcf > HIGH_HOM.vcf`.

steps.title: Optional: Confirm region and narrow SNPs
steps.instruction: Validate the mapping interval using indel markers and narrow candidate SNPs.

substeps.instruction: Extract the mapping region again (same awk command as before).
Identify homozygous indels: `grep HOM=1 chr1_mapping_region.vcf > chr1_mapping_region_HOM.vcf`.
Select indels ≥10 bp, design primers flanking each indel, PCR amplify, and run products on a 3.5 % agarose gel. Band‑size differences confirm background genotype.

steps.title: Annotate Moderate and High effect genes
steps.instruction: Link SNPs to gene annotations using the maize gene function file.

substeps.instruction: Download gene annotations from ftp://ftp.gramene.org/pub/gramene/CURRENT_RELEASE/gff3/zea_mays/gene_function (file B73v4.gene_function.txt).
Extract gene IDs from VCFs: `awk -F'|' '{print $5}' MODERATE.vcf > MODERATE_filter1.vcf` then `awk -F':' '{print $2}' MODERATE_filter1.vcf > MODERATE_gene_IDs.txt` (repeat for HIGH).
Retrieve gene descriptions: `grep -wf MODERATE_gene_IDs.txt B73v4.gene_function.txt` (and similarly for HIGH).

steps.title: Optional: Assess SNP impact with PROVEAN
steps.instruction: Submit Moderate SNP protein sequences to the PROVEAN web server (http://provean.jcvi.org/seq_submit.php) to predict deleteriousness (≈77.9 % accuracy). Note that PROVEAN is low‑throughput for non‑human genomes.

description: Phase 2 Overview To plot homozygous SNPs in our filtered pileup file, we use the R packages dplyr and ggplot2 in R studio. Before plotting, we first change the format of our filtered pileup file to make it easy to manipulate in R studio. Then we use dplyr to remove background SNPs in the data. And finally, we plot our data as binned homozygous SNPs along each chromosome. Remove background SNPs chr1_final_NoWT <- anti_join(chr1_final, WT_chr1, by='position') chr1_final_NoWTHapmap <- anti_join(chr1_final_NoWT, Hapmap_chr1, by='position')
